suggestions: Replace Rank of a product with an equal-weight average of separate cross-sectional ranks, then apply one smoother: Ma((Rank(Ma((close-low)/(high-low), 5) - Ma((close-low)/(high-low), 20)) + Rank(Tanh(Zscore(volume, 20)))) / 2, 10). Ranking the multiplicative blend forces tail stocks to dominate differently each day and creates hidden interaction terms (rank of a product) that are easy to overfit when IC is near zero; averaging two independent ranks keeps the same economic story—range-position momentum confirmed by elevated volume—without letting a few extreme products drive the cross-section every rebalance.

Remove the stacked outer smoothers Ma(..., 20) then Ma(..., 3) and use a single mid-horizon average on the ranked signal: Ma(Rank((Ma((close-low)/(high-low), 5) - Ma((close-low)/(high-low), 20)) * Tanh(Zscore(volume, 20))), 10). The fast 3-day outer layer mainly retrains reactivity to daily rank reversals and turnover (~1.0) rather than adding new information about conviction; paired with the inner 3/20 spread it creates four tunable horizons (3, 20, 20, 3) that can fit in-sample micro-reversals without improving validation RankIR, which is a classic overfitting signature when effectiveness stays at zero.

Replace Tanh(Zscore(volume, 20)) with a nonparametric volume leg Rank(Delta(volume, 5) / Ma(volume, 20), 20): Ma(Rank((Ma((close-low)/(high-low), 5) - Ma((close-low)/(high-low), 20)) * Rank(Delta(volume, 5) / Ma(volume, 20), 20)), 10). Z-score plus Tanh assumes a stable volume distribution and squashes tails in a way that varies across volatility regimes, adding nonlinear parameters that the optimizer can tune to historical volume spikes; a cross-sectional rank of recent volume change relative to its baseline captures the same 'unusually active today' idea with fewer distributional assumptions and less risk of fitting idiosyncratic volume tail behavior.
